# The mosaic aneuploidy bound — hypothesis board

**Goal.** Is mosaic aneuploidy detectable in the sequenced sample with a statistic that has power, and what cell-fraction bound does the data set per chromosome?

| ID | Status | Confidence | Gene | Evidence | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [H051](h051-step-8.md) | supported | 0.80 | — | 2+ / 0− | No chromosome in the sequenced sample -- autosome or X -- carries a mosaic aneuploidy at a cell fraction above its own measured detection limit. |
| [H052](h052-step-8.md) | supported | 0.85 | — | 1+ / 0− | The detection limit of the fold-over B-deviation test is at most 10 percent cell fraction for every autosome at this sample's heterozygous-site count and depth. |
| [H053](h053-step-8.md) | supported | 0.95 | — | 2+ / 0− | Fold-over B-deviation detects a mosaic gain at a materially lower cell fraction than the mean B-allele-fraction statistic entry 037 used, on identical simulated sites. |
| [H054](h054-step-8.md) | supported | 0.85 | — | 3+ / 0− | The k-mer dosage route and the VCF allele-balance route agree on every chromosome within their stated intervals. |
| [H055](h055-step-8.md) | supported | 0.80 | — | 2+ / 0− | The leave-one-chromosome-out baseline is stable: no chromosome's exclusion moves the genome-wide baseline beyond its bootstrap interval. |
| [H056](h056-step-8.md) | supported | 0.85 | — | 2+ / 0− | The mixing simulation recovers two and three simultaneously affected chromosomes at 10 and 20 percent cell fraction, and does not flag the unaffected ones. |
| [H057](h057-step-8.md) | supported | 0.85 | — | 2+ / 0− | Mitotic and meiotic trisomy are not separable at delta-BIC of 10 or more from arm-stratified allele-fraction band structure at cell fractions up to 20 percent, at this sample's depth and heterozygous-site counts. |
